turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): I do apologize for being late, Doctor. The parking structure was full and, um, we circled for quite a while.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, the third floor was a total mess. We almost just went home.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're here. What brings you in?
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, my neighbor has been quite persistent, actually. Her cousin was diagnosed with a thyroid condition, and she said I looked washed out and ought to come in.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not my patient. What's wrong with you?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): I've been so tired. That is truly why I made this appointment.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, maybe three months. Well, actually, roughly two months. I cannot say the exact day it began, I'm afraid.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. On the stairs at the office. One flight and, uh, I have to stop.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? Any wheeze?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No cough, and no wheeze.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dizzy?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's chewing ice all evening, Doc. Whole cups of it. Kind of weird.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): That is correct. I have been craving ice. I am rather embarrassed to say so.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Periods heavy?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. They are normal. Regular, not heavy.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vegetarian?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, strictly so. No meat and, well, actually no fish either, for six years. I do still eat eggs and dairy.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): None. I am not taking a medicine or a vitamin.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I should add, last spring the campus clinic said my iron was borderline. I never went back. That was foolish of me.
[SEG0026] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry, popping in. Pressure's 108 over 68, heart rate 92, oxygen sat 99 percent.
[SEG0027] person_4 (NURSE): My sister was anemic after her second kid. Lived on spinach smoothies for months. We got so tired of it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Look up. Conjunctiva are pale. Tongue's pale too.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds normal. No murmur.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Very likely low iron. The blood isn't carrying oxygen the way it should. That's why the stairs wipe you out, and the ice craving fits.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I see. Would there be a treatment for that?
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Labs first. CBC and a ferritin, today. Front desk books the draw.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the ferritin's low I may start feros sulfate. Not before that.
[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just so you know, she will not eat liver. Don't even try.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): No liver. Lentils, tofu, spinach, beans. Orange juice with them, for the vitamin C. Every day.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I will do that. Thank you, Doctor.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight loss?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): No. My weight has stayed the same.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Back in two weeks. We look at the numbers then.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you for fitting us in, even with the late arrival. I appreciate it.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Tiredness and roughly two months supported; 'certainty=uncertain' is wrong because symptom itself is stated clearly.
